findings.problem: Lines 52–70 are a non-trivial argument that is repeated almost verbatim in RS.karoubiHom_eq_zero_of_traces_vanish (Novel/Envelope/KaroubiSemisimple.lean, lines 92–122). The argument has four parts. First, it shows that Y.p ≫ b ≫ X.p is a Karoubi morphism, via the idempotence proof `hb`. Second, it proves `hred`, that a.f ≫ (p ≫ b ≫ p) = (a.f ≫ b) ≫ p. Third, it uses p_comp to insert the idempotent. Fourth, it uses cyclicity to move the idempotent across. The calc chain is the same. Only the trace function differs, and it enters only through its cyclicity. Any change to the argument, or any new corner-trace result, must be made twice. The generic fact, that a trace-like cyclic function cannot distinguish a.f ≫ b from its corner-compressed version, is buried inside two long proofs.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma in KaroubiTrace.lean, which the other file already imports. It is stated for any category and any cyclic function.

theorem karoubi_exists_corner_eq {C : Type*} [Category C] {X Y : Karoubi C} {M : Type*} (τ : (X.X ⟶ X.X) → M) (hcyc : ∀ u v : X.X ⟶ X.X, τ (u ≫ v) = τ (v ≫ u)) (a : X ⟶ Y) (b : Y.X ⟶ X.X) : ∃ c : Y ⟶ X, τ (a.f ≫ b) = τ (a.f ≫ c.f)

Proof sketch:
1. Take c := ⟨Y.p ≫ b ≫ X.p, hb⟩, where hb is the existing idempotence computation. It uses Y.idem and X.idem.
2. Run the existing calc: τ (a.f ≫ b) = τ (X.p ≫ (a.f ≫ b)) by Karoubi.p_comp, then = τ ((a.f ≫ b) ≫ X.p) by hcyc, then = τ (a.f ≫ (Y.p ≫ b ≫ X.p)) by hred.

Use in the target, replacing lines 53–70:
  intro b
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := karoubi_exists_corner_eq (X := P) (Y := P) τ hcyc a b
  rw [hc]; exact ha c

Use in KaroubiSemisimple.lean, replacing lines 92–122:
  intro b
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := karoubi_exists_corner_eq (X := X) (Y := Y) (HomSpace.traceMap f.val X.X.arity) (fun u v => HomSpace.traceMap_comp_comm f (t := X.X.arity) (u := X.X.arity) u v) a b
  rw [hc]; exact ha c

The `ha` hypotheses are the ones already in scope. In the target, `ha` is applied to End P elements. In the other file, it is applied to Y ⟶ X morphisms.
findings.benefit: The roughly 20-line corner-compression argument is written and maintained once. Each user shrinks to about three lines and states only its trace-specific hypothesis, which is cyclicity. A reader sees that the corner restriction needs nothing beyond cyclicity and the Karoubi idempotent laws. The lemma is also available to any future trace on a Karoubi corner.
